messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: Continuous Batcher Latency Spike detected for pool 'eu-west-1-batcher' — P2. alert: 95th p50 p95 p99 latency jump +800% and error rate for /v1/generate increased to 12% :warning:

sam_w: seeing the same on grafana. queues are growing, nodes in that pool are flapping. CUDA OOMs on two pods. paging rate spiked. :fire:

maya_r: customer ticket #CS-8812 reporting multiple timeouts and 500s since 13:02 UTC. large enterprise customer impacted (low volume but high SLAs).

jordan_k: logs from pod runtime-batcher-7 show repeated OOM then restartBackOff:
```
[13:03:12] RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 12.00 GiB (GPU 0; 14.73 GiB total capacity)
[13:03:13] Container restarted (OOMKilled)
[13:03:14] Paging: swapped 1.2GiB to host, continuous-batcher queue length 18k
```

lee_ops: confirmed kube events: kubelet evicting due to memory pressure on node ip-10-2-5-21. node flaps twice in 3m and kubelet died once.

nora_a: initial triage — looks like a combination of continuous-batcher growth + KV cache retention causing a working set explosion under a recent runtime change (seq-length heuristics). suspect regression from yesterday's deploy (runtime v3.12.4).

sam_w: mitigation plan: 1) disable continuous batching on the impacted model variant 2) enable emergency queue throttle 3) cordon/fluid-restart flapping nodes 4) roll back v3.12.4 if needed.

maya_r: can someone flip throttle first? customer impact ongoing. I'll open a bridge.

jordan_k: throttling endpoint in console responded: POST /admin/batcher/throttle {"mode":"emergency","ratio":0.2} — returned 200. Applying now.

incident-bot: Action taken: emergency throttle enabled for pool 'eu-west-1-batcher' by jordan_k at 13:07:23 UTC.

lee_ops: after throttle: queue length dropped from 18k -> 3.5k over 90s, p95 latency improved from 7.2s -> 2.1s, error rate down to 4%. but still seeing pod OOMs on two nodes.

nora_a: next: scale down model batch size and disable continuous batching on that model. sam_w can you patch runtime config?

sam_w: applying runtime patch to disable continuous batching for model redwood-rt-7b-v1 in the affected pool. patch payload:
```json
{"model":"redwood-rt-7b-v1","continuous_batching":false}
```

incident-bot: Patch request accepted; rollout to pool 'eu-west-1-batcher' initiated.

jordan_k: also pushed a temporary cgroup memory cap on pods to limit runaway KV cache: kubectl patch deployment batcher --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"batcher","resources":{"limits":{"memory":"10Gi"}}}]}}}}' -n runtime

lee_ops: FYI node ip-10-2-5-21 still flapping; cordoned and drained. moving remaining pods off to healthy nodes.

maya_r: customer updated: "saw intermittent 500s for ~10min, then partial recovery. still seeing timeouts for large prompts." they want RCA and ETA.

nora_a: we should consider rollback if deploy is culprit. Anyone seen related commits? I see a hotfix yesterday that changed seq-length batching heuristics (PR #4123).

sam_w: rolling back PR #4123 in runtime v3.12.4 -> v3.12.3 for eu-west-1 pool only. initiating canary rollback on 1 instance then broad.

incident-bot: Rollback started by sam_w at 13:14:40 UTC. Canary instance patched.

jordan_k: post-rollback metrics look promising on canary: no OOMs, KV resident memory down ~35%, steady queue. scheduling broad rollback now.

lee_ops: performing rolling restart on remaining flappy nodes after drain, marking some nodes as unsched until kubelet restart and kernel reprovisioning.

maya_r: running quick smoke tests against customer flows — large prompt test passed once, still occasional serialization latency but acceptable for now. sending update to CS.

nora_a: next steps for full mitigation notes for postmortem: - confirm root cause (seq-length heuristics memory growth under certain prefix distributions) - add automated circuit breaker to disable continuous batching if queue > X or if page rate > Y - add metric to track KV resident set per model - add e2e test for large prompt tails - add memory guardrails in runtime and coordination with schedulers

sam_w: also plan to backfill emergency regression alert when deploy changes batch heuristics. filing followup ticket: INF-8292.

jordan_k: final status: emergency throttle + disable continuous batching + rollback + node stabilization returned the pool to normal at 13:27 UTC. marking incident as mitigated.

incident-bot: INCIDENT MITIGATED: Continuous Batcher Latency Spike — P2. duration ~24m. Please fill incident form: /incidents/new?ref=2245123456

maya_r: handoff to next oncall: @lee_ops you're up for postmortem write-up and customer comms. I will keep an eye during my overlap. :eyes:

lee_ops: ack. collecting logs and trace links, will draft timeline and RCA.

nora_a: thanks all — great quick work. we'll schedule a postmortem and follow-ups. :thumbsup:
